title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.
summary: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court.

Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home." title: Residents asked to pick site for new zebra crossing in Huntingdonshire town
content: Residents are being asked to help decide where a new zebra crossing should be installed in Ramsey as part of plans to improve pedestrian safety and accessibility in the town. Cambridgeshire County Council is asking residents to choose between two possible sites for the crossing. The proposed locations are: Residents have two sites to choose from one is on High Street, opposite Ramsey Abbey Gatehouse, the other is on Hollow Lane opposite Ramsey Golf and Bowls Club. (Image: Google Maps / Street View) The council said the results of the survey, which runs until midnight on Wednesday, October 28, will be considered alongside other highway, safety and accessibility information before a final decision is made. Residents, students, parents, carers and regular pedestrians are all being encouraged to take part. The council says residents’ views will help identify the safest and most effective site for people travelling on foot. An engagement survey has been opened to gather views on the proposals. Councillors have voted to refuse a controversial 199-home development plan for Ramsey despite receiving a recommendation for approval. BDW Trading Ltd submitted the proposal for land south of The Malting with landowners Susan and Robert Pickard. The scheme included up to 199 homes, 40 per cent affordable housing, children’s play areas, drainage infrastructure and related works. Developers also proposed a landscaped perimeter, a 1.1km circular walking route linked to public rights of way and green infrastructure covering around 37 per cent of the site. The site is land south of The Malting in Ramsey However, at a meeting on October 19, Huntingdonshire District Council's Development Management Committee voted to refuse the outline application, which had been recommended for approval.
